reuse.why: Extracts a real shared linkBankSyncAccount used by all six providers, but copies downloadAkahuTransactions for Fintegra and re-writes unlinkAccount's link-clearing update instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: The holders query appears twice (assertBankAccountNotLinked and releaseExistingLinks), the closed-account check twice (assert helper and linkBankSyncAccount), the unlink field-clearing block copies unlinkAccount, and downloadFintegraTransactions copies the Akahu downloader.

placement.why: Link logic stays in accounts/app.ts, but assertBankAccountNotLinked now also enforces the closed-account rule and the take-over is a closure inside the link helper, blurring responsibilities.

scope.why: Changes stay on the four linking steps and the Fintegra provider, plus type-forced client entries and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared link helper is a clear win, but rule checks are split and repeated between a misnamed assert function and the helper, and the downloader is another verbatim copy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: releaseExistingLinks in linkBankSyncAccount re-implements unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount clearing instead of a shared unlink helper; downloadFintegraTransactions repeats the existing provider downloader rather than generalising it.

disguised_duplication.where: The link-clearing update is moved into a nested releaseExistingLinks closure, and the holders query is reshaped (first ... LIMIT 1 vs all) between assertBankAccountNotLinked and releaseExistingLinks in accounts/app.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: replaceExistingLink added to both linkBankSyncAccount and assertBankAccountNotLinked; a closed-account branch and a releaseExistingLinks branch added inside linkBankSyncAccount (the closed check also lives in assertBankAccountNotLinked); every provider handler calls the helper.
